entities.evidence: Adam is the father who names his son Seth, matching the Adam who fathered Seth with Eve in Genesis 4:25.
Seth is the name Adam gives his son here. Genesis 4:25 identifies Seth as the son of Adam and Eve born after Abel’s death.

review.translation: [And|0] [Adam|1] [lived|0] [130|3,2] [years|4], [then he fathered|5] {a son} [in his own likeness|6], [according to his image|7], [and he called|8] [his name|10,9] [Seth|11].

analysis.evidence: אָדָם is the subject of וַיְחִי, and שְׁלֹשִׁים וּמְאַת שָׁנָה gives the duration. Adam lived 130 years before he fathered Seth.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix
analysis.sense: live for a stated length of time

analysis.evidence: וַיְחִי אָדָם names Adam as the subject. The verse gives his age as 130 years when he fathered a son and named him Seth.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun, without article, prefix, or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In שְׁלֹשִׁים וּמְאַת שָׁנָה, the conjunction וּ joins thirty and one hundred. Together they give Adam’s age of 130 years when he fathered Seth.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, common gender, plural, absolute state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: מְאַת governs שָׁנָה ‘year’ in the construct phrase מְאַת שָׁנָה ‘a hundred years’. The conjunction joins this count to שְׁלֹשִׁים ‘thirty’, giving Adam’s age as 130 years.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ ‘and’ prefixed to מְאַת, the singular construct form of the cardinal numeral מֵאָה.

analysis.evidence: With וַיְחִי אָדָם ‘Adam lived’, שְׁלֹשִׁים וּמְאַת שָׁנָה gives Adam’s age in years when he fathered Seth. The singular שָׁנָה supplies the unit for the count of 130.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Adam is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד. The child is described as being in Adam’s likeness and image, and Adam names him Seth.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: The suffix refers to Adam. The parallel phrase כְּצַלְמוֹ, “according to his image,” reinforces that Seth bears his father’s likeness.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בִּ־ plus feminine singular construct noun with third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ.

analysis.evidence: כְּצַלְמוֹ parallels בִּדְמוּתוֹ (“in his likeness”). Both suffixes refer to Adam, who fathered Seth, so the phrase describes Seth’s resemblance to his father.
analysis.morphology: Comparative preposition כְּ + masculine singular construct noun + third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ referring to Adam.

analysis.evidence: Adam is the subject of וַיִּקְרָא. The marked direct object אֶת שְׁמוֹ means “his name,” and שֵׁת supplies the name Adam gave his son.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקְרָא אֶת שְׁמוֹ שֵׁת, “he called his name Seth,” אֶת marks שְׁמוֹ (“his name”) as the direct object of וַיִּקְרָא. The possessive suffix makes שְׁמוֹ definite, and שֵׁת supplies the name given.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle, without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Genesis 5:3 as an example of the first Hebrew noun sense in the existing shem article.
draft.definition: The personal name by which someone is known.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:3 supplies the child's name, שֵׁת, immediately after שְׁמוֹ, “his name.”

patch.value: Adam calls his son's name Seth. The word שְׁמוֹ refers to the personal name he gives the child.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּקְרָא אֶת שְׁמוֹ שֵׁת, Adam calls his son's name Seth. The suffix ־וֹ refers to the son just born, and שֵׁת gives the name Adam assigns him.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ.
analysis.sense: name by which someone is known

analysis.evidence: וַיִּקְרָא אֶת שְׁמוֹ שֵׁת means “he called his name Seth.” The suffix in שְׁמוֹ refers to the son Adam has just fathered, and שֵׁת gives the child’s name.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: the son of Adam and his wife born after Abel’s death
